text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Singapore-Boston business alliance signed on Wednesday is the first of an anticipated network of linkages which will bring the Republic and major American regions into closer collaboration on education, high technology and international trade.
- Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan resigned after weathering six tumultuous months in office, leaving behind a hot seat with few takers and an economy mired in uncertainty.
- PIDEMCO Land and MCL Land sealed their first joint deal yesterday to develop a Singapore $800 million industrial property in Kampong Ubi.
- Asian banks have been urged to join hands and forge alliances to tap more business opportunities in the region's increasingly competitive environment.
- Singapore's Budget Day will be held in the first half of July, says Finance Minister Richard Hu.
- Construction, property and hotel group Lim Kah Ngam has obtained provisional permission to redevelop Hotel Equatorial in Bukit Timah Road into a condominium, setting the stage for its sale.
- Singapore is committed to supporting the Thai baht and sees Thailand's economic problems as temporary, Finance Minister Richard Hu said yesterday.

- The Malaysian Ang family that controls a strategic stake in Singapore-listed Parkway Holdings is expected to decide soon whether to sell its 13.5 percent block to DBS Land, which is widely seen to be poised for a takeover of the healthcare group.
- The proposed bridge linking Malaysia and Indonesia will be built from Malacca to Dumai in southern Sumatra and is expected to cost M$6 billion officials said on Wednesday.
- Goldman Sachs Group reported a 19 percent rise in earnings before taxes to US$1.52 billion for the six months ended May 31.
- Qantas Airways threatened an "aggressive response" to what it called an imminent equity partnership between Singapore Airlines and Australia's Ansett Airlines.
- The plaintiffs and at least two of the three defendants in the Jumabhoy case are claiming victory in the High Court judgement delivered on Wednesday.
